question: Should OpenClaw support an experimental embedded-agent opt-in that sends one archived reset-family compaction summary to the selected model provider, and should it land only after the explicit family-history PR?
rationale: The patch is intentionally default-off and has focused evidence, but choosing whether reset archives may cross the model-provider boundary is a product and privacy contract decision rather than a mechanical correction.

options.title: Land as a stacked opt-in
options.body: Accept the archived-context provider boundary, land the prerequisite family-history contract first, then rebase and validate this PR as the explicit experimental carryover layer.

options.title: Keep family retrieval only
options.body: Land or retain explicit `includeFamily` retrieval while declining automatic prompt carryover, leaving archived context available only when a caller requests it.

options.title: Redesign the boundary
options.body: Require a narrower provider policy or a user-visible consent surface before any archived summary can enter embedded-agent prompts.

recommendation.title: Land as a stacked opt-in
recommendation.body: Accept the archived-context provider boundary, land the prerequisite family-history contract first, then rebase and validate this PR as the explicit experimental carryover layer.

likelyOwner.reason: The discussion specifically asks this person to route the stack order and provider-boundary choice.
